skills.name: Parallel Task Completion Polling
skills.description: Wait for one or more Futures to complete with configurable timeout and return condition. Supports three completion modes: return when any task finishes (FIRST_COMPLETED), return when any task raises an exception (FIRST_EXCEPTION), or return when all tasks finish (ALL_COMPLETED). Use to synchronize on parallel task outcomes and partition results into done and pending sets.
skills.skill_body:
Call concurrent.futures.wait(fs, timeout=None, return_when=ALL_COMPLETED) with a collection of Future objects. Specify timeout in seconds (int or float) to limit wait duration; None means no limit. Choose return_when constant to control early exit: FIRST_COMPLETED returns immediately when any Future finishes or is cancelled; FIRST_EXCEPTION returns when any Future raises an exception (or behaves like ALL_COMPLETED if none raise); ALL_COMPLETED waits for all Futures to finish or be cancelled. The function returns a tuple (done, pending) where done is a set of completed Futures and pending is a set of Futures still running.

## Objective

coordinate multi-task synchronization
## Applicable Signals

- Multiple Futures submitted to ThreadPoolExecutor or ProcessPoolExecutor
- Synchronization point required before inspecting or processing results
- Timeout constraint or early-exit condition specified by caller

## Contraindications

- Non-blocking polling is preferred; use as_completed() iterator instead
- No timeout constraint and caller can iterate over results as they arrive
- Single Future result retrieval; use Future.result() directly

## Workflow Steps

- Prepare a collection of Future objects from submitted tasks
- Determine timeout value (seconds) or None for no limit
- Select return_when constant based on synchronization strategy
- Call concurrent.futures.wait(fs, timeout, return_when)
- Unpack returned (done, pending) tuple
- Iterate over done set to retrieve results or handle exceptions
- If pending is non-empty, decide whether to retry, cancel, or log

## Constraints

- fs parameter must be a non-empty collection of Future objects
- timeout must be None, int, or float; negative values are treated as zero
- return_when must be one of the three module constants: FIRST_COMPLETED, FIRST_EXCEPTION, or ALL_COMPLETED
- Function may raise TimeoutError if timeout is exceeded and no Futures have completed

## Cautions

- TimeoutError is a deprecated alias of built-in TimeoutError as of Python 3.11
- If a Future is cancelled before wait() returns, it appears in the done set
- FIRST_EXCEPTION mode returns immediately only if an exception is raised; if no exception occurs, it waits like ALL_COMPLETED

## Output Contract

- Returns a tuple (done, pending) where done is a set of Futures that have completed (finished, raised exception, or were cancelled) and pending is a set of Futures still running. Caller can call Future.result() or Future.exception() on items in done to retrieve outcomes. If timeout is exceeded before return condition is met, raises TimeoutError.
